The arbiter writes the result unconditionally: sender.rs:3588 `let (final_ratio, reason) = fec_arbiter(confirmed, structure, spec);` and sender.rs:3621 `d.fec_parity_ratio_permille = final_ratio;` — neither is state-gated. The full enumeration of PreConverge guards in sender.rs (grep 'PreConverge') shows the ONLY FEC-side guard is sender.rs:3663-3665 inside structure_gate_fec. Default is ON: crates/client-core/src/runtime.rs:204 `fec_loss_risk: FecLossRiskConfig::bounded_v1(),` and sender.rs:437 `enabled: true,` with sender.rs:407 `l1_min_instant_ppm: 10_000` (1% loss). Reachability: the ledger DOES accumulate in PreConverge because LossDetector::on_ack is ungated (sender.rs:3004) and calls declare() (loss.rs:661), and ledger_tick is likewise ungated (sender.rs:3394-3395) so Suspected→Confirmed promotion happens there too (loss.rs:338-341); Confirmed events contribute to instant_ppm regardless of srtt (loss.rs:418-421), unlike Suspected which needs srtt != 0 (loss.rs:424). A PreConverge session that receives a SACK covering only a §3.3-B copy or an establish probe (TransmitKind::Duplicate) gets NO RTT sample under Karn (sender.rs:2951) and therefore STAYS in PreConverge while its ledger fills — the exact state in which the speculative lane can fire. This directly defeats the guard's own stated rationale (sender.rs:3655-3662: parity 'kıt token bütçesinde ORİJİNALLERLE yarışıyor ve ilk-uçuş orijinal sayısını düşürerek kuruluş olasılığını kırıyordu'). Currently inert ONLY because RuntimeConfig::default() has fec: None → FecActuationMode::Manual{enabled:false} → sender.rs:4606 `FecActuationMode::Manual { .. } => zero(0, FecSuppressionReason::ManualDisabled, false)`. Any FEC-enabled arm removes that protection.
missed_mechanisms.suggested_classification: WIRE (v1 blocker for any FEC-enabled configuration: the PreConverge guard must cover the arbiter output, not just the structure gate). Audit-only observation; no reopening of the FEC v1 closure research is implied.

missed_mechanisms.name: Confirmed/fuzzy FEC lane also lacks a PreConverge guard (same latch, same reachability)
missed_mechanisms.evidence: In fuzzy_evaluate the canonical decision `d` is computed from FusionInputs including inputs.loss_ppm before any state check, and its fec_parity_ratio_permille feeds fec_arbiter as `confirmed` (crates/adaptive-transport/src/sender.rs:3588). loss_ppm derives from the same ledger that fills during PreConverge (loss.rs:661 via ungated sender.rs:3004). No SenderState::PreConverge test exists anywhere between the fuzzy decision and sender.rs:3621. The BlockedPreConverge outcome is only ever returned from structure_gate_fec (sender.rs:3663-3665), which by construction runs only when fuzzy already left fec at 0 (sender.rs:3650-3652 `if fuzzy_fec_permille != 0 { return GateOutcome::NotApplicable; }`) — i.e. the guard is unreachable precisely in the case where fuzzy itself opened parity.
missed_mechanisms.suggested_classification: WIRE (same defect class as above; the guard's placement makes it structurally incapable of covering the fuzzy branch)

missed_mechanisms.name: Three cold-start mechanisms ship default-ON with NO RuntimeConfig knob — establish probe, startup pacing floor, §3.3-B copy schedule
missed_mechanisms.evidence: crates/adaptive-transport/src/sender.rs:1819 `establish_probe_enabled: true,` (setter set_establish_probe at :5598 has 13 call sites, all tests); sender.rs:1125 `Self { enabled: true }` for StartupPacingConfig (setter set_startup_pacing_init at :2019 has 9 call sites, all tests); the §3.3-B schedule at sender.rs:5693-5707 has no config at all. RuntimeConfig (crates/client-core/src/runtime.rs:95-207) exposes none of the three. Two of them additionally conflict with normative spec text (establish probe vs specs/adaptive-transport-engine-spec.md:332-333; startup floor absent from the frozen spec entirely). Consequence: transport tests that disable these to isolate other mechanisms run a configuration the product can never be placed in, and an operator has no way to revert to spec-conformant behaviour without a code change.
missed_mechanisms.suggested_classification: SHIP for all three (they are wired and default-enabled), but flagged as a governance gap: default-ON + no product switch + unamended spec

missed_mechanisms.name: Bench arm/product default divergence is not limited to [IW] — the kama-product bench arm cannot exercise several shipping cold-start defaults
missed_mechanisms.evidence: crates/bench/src/kama_product.rs:147-180 constructs RuntimeConfig with explicit field initializers rather than `..Default::default()` for the cold-start axes, taking initial_window_bytes (main.rs:123-124, default 0), bootstrap_rtt (main.rs:120-121, default false) and bootstrap_fast (main.rs:126-127, default false) from the CLI. For initial_window_bytes this means the CLI default (0) overrides the shipping default (2400, runtime.rs:195) on every bench run unless the flag is passed. The in-tree help text compounds this: crates/bench/src/main.rs:122 and :237 both say '0 = sevk davranışı, tek paket', and crates/bench/src/kama_product.rs:160 says '[IW] opt-in; 0 = sevk davranışı' — all three assert the opposite of runtime.rs:195.
missed_mechanisms.suggested_classification: Not a mechanism — a measurement-validity defect. Any cold-start number produced by the kama-product arm without --initial-window-bytes 2400 describes a configuration the product does not ship.

corrected_classifications.mechanism: [IW] Initial window / first-flight budget in PreConverge (InitialWindowConfig, RuntimeConfig.initial_window_bytes)
corrected_classifications.reason: KEEP-EXPERIMENTAL requires default OFF by this audit's own definition; the product default is ON at 2400 B (crates/client-core/src/runtime.rs:195), wired through the sole product call site at runtime.rs:856-858 into sender.rs:2234-2242, and pinned by crates/client-core/tests/runtime_e2e.rs:762. It is therefore shipped, not experimental. The label change does not resolve the substantive conflict the finding correctly identified: the ON default contradicts normative [K-D2] (specs/adaptive-transport-engine-spec.md:303) and the transport crate's own 'KALİBRE EDİLMEMİŞ' note (sender.rs:315). Under CLAUDE.md §3 (spec wins) the owner must either amend [K-D2] via D0→D1 or flip runtime.rs:195 to 0. Classifying it KEEP-EXPERIMENTAL would misreport a live shipping default as inert.

corrected_classifications.mechanism: DR-CS-1 M2/F2A legacy CS-probe ladder lane (experimental-cold-start feature)
corrected_classifications.reason: The reachability analysis is confirmed (product-unreachable in both configurations: runtime.rs:837 + sender.rs:4085-4088), but DELETE requires dead/obsolete AND removable. This lane is not compiled in the default build (crates/adaptive-transport/Cargo.toml feature default OFF; client-core does not forward it), is byte-identical when off, and is the load-bearing control arm of crates/kama-integration/tests/common/dr_cs3_panel.rs and tests/dr_cs1_acceptance.rs — which the finding itself concedes must be re-targeted first. That is exactly the KEEP-EXPERIMENTAL contract: default OFF, not secretly needed for v1 claims. Reclassify to DELETE only after the panel is re-targeted; recording it as DELETE now overstates what can be removed without breaking the DR-CS-3 evidence chain.

Product-unreachability is confirmed (kama-integration has zero workspace dependents; grep of crates/*/Cargo.toml). But it is the only implementation that satisfies the DR-CS-3 contract receiver §16-18 budget (MAX_ECHOES / ECHO_BUDGET_BYTES), which the product responder at crates/client-core/src/runtime.rs:2311-2323 does NOT enforce. Deleting the conformant reference while shipping the non-conformant responder inverts the risk: the correct sequence is to fold the ≤4-echo/172-byte budget into ServerEndpoint before bootstrap_rtt could ever flip ON, and only then remove. Keep it default-scoped to kama-integration until that lands.

Absence is confirmed (0 repo-wide hits), but WIRE asserts a v1 blocker and the spec does not support that reading for single-path v1. specs/adaptive-transport-engine-spec.md:883-885 defines PATH_DEAD as escalation to failover and explicitly prescribes, for the no-alternative-hub case, the continued low-tempo geometric queue the code already implements. With no failover target in v1 scope there is no consumer for the state. Treat as deferred/out-of-v1 pending the owner's [K6]/TV-COLDSTART-5 scope decision rather than as a disconnected required mechanism; it becomes WIRE the moment multipath enters v1.
